tables.placement: Embedded in main text near discussion; not at end, not separate files.
tables.title_caption_position_numbering: Label 'TABLE 1' centered, all caps; short descriptive title centered, all caps, no final period; cite in text as lowercase 'table 1'.
tables.notes_conventions: Notes cued by lowercase superscript letters at bottom below the rule, paragraph-indented; descriptive information placed above the notes; source lines at bottom, indented, left-aligned.
tables.significance_stars: not specified for tables; style guide requires specific p-values (p = .035 rather than p < .05); significant if p < .05, 'marginally significant' if .05-.10, not significant if > .10, always with exact p; 'approaching/directionally significant' banned; NS abbreviation.
tables.uncertainty_reporting: CIs: '95% CI [.03, .57]'; CIs may be two columns in a table; error bars (optional) must be 95% CIs; report effect sizes when appropriate. SE not specified.
tables.decimals_leading_zero: Decimals aligned in columns; no zero before decimal point in probabilities (p = .035); other leading-zero use not specified.
tables.heading_capitalization: Sentence-style: only the initial letter of a word/phrase/column head capitalized; every column must have a heading.
tables.font_size: Sans serif only (Helvetica, Arial); size not specified.
tables.landscape_allowed: Yes for individual tables/figures (rest of manuscript portrait).

figures.file_formats: .ai, .bmp, .eps, .gif, .pdf, .png, .ppt/.pptx, .ps, .raw, .tif/.tiff, .xls/.xlsx; source files (Excel/PowerPoint) preferred for charts/flowcharts.
figures.min_resolution: not specified (review: low-res encouraged; acceptance: 'higher-resolution' images).
figures.color_policy: Color online free; color print charged by OUP (choose at proof stage, B/W print free).
figures.fonts: Sans serif only (Helvetica, Arial), legible at actual print size; min size not specified.
figures.caption_position: Label 'FIGURE 1' and title centered, all caps, in the manuscript (above figure per sample); omitted from the separate figure files.
figures.placement: Embedded in main text (review and final) plus separate file per figure at acceptance.
figures.figure_notes: Notes and source lines at bottom, indented, left-aligned; descriptive info above notes.
figures.other_rules: Label both axes; y-axis label centered above axis; x-axis label flush right beneath axis; ticks inside axis lines, values outside; single zero at origin; legends horizontal in white space or centered beneath; distinguish lines by bold/fine/broken/dotted; minimize white space inside boxes; error bars = 95% CI.

tables.editable_text_required: yes: the INFORMS Author Portal says tabular data should be editable tables, not images. The informs4 documentation allows an extremely complex table to be set as vector artwork.
tables.placement: not specified on the MNSC page, which could not be read directly (see other_notable). The informs4 template places tables as floats in the text.
tables.caption: Above the table, in title case, after a bold number with a period, running in, with no final period. Example: 'Table 1. Determinants of Director Equity Deferrals: Multiple-Board Directors'. Arabic numerals. Each table must be cited in the text in numerical order, with 'Table' spelled out. If the caption runs past one sentence, the extra sentences become a Note; footnotes may not be attached to captions. (INFORMS Style Guide v1.7; the informs4 documentation says the caption is always set above the table body.)
tables.notes: Order below the table: 'Source.' (italic heading) first; then 'Note.' or 'Notes.' (italic heading), with abbreviation definitions last in the format 'IHP, infinite horizon problem; CCM, ...'; then footnotes. Each footnote sits on its own line with a superscript symbol (a, b, ...) and a 1-em indent. Multiple p-value notes go on one line separated by semicolons.
tables.significance_stars: Allowed. The INFORMS Style Guide's own example footnote reads '*p < 0.01; **p < 0.05; ***p < 0.001' (verbatim, ordering as printed). Put spaces around '<' (p < 0.01). Write 'p-value' with a hyphen. Exact p-values are not required and no thresholds are mandated.
tables.rules_shading: Three horizontal rules only: below the caption (above the column heads), below the column heads, and below the body. Use as few rules as possible. Straddle rules (cline) are acceptable. No vertical rules by default; they can be reinserted at the author's request.
tables.decimals_leading_zero: Leading zero required for all values below 1 (for example, p < 0.001). Decimal-align data in the table body. Use commas in numbers of 4 or more digits (1,000). Use en dashes for ranges and center em dashes. Write R2, not 'R-squared'.
tables.headings: The first column head is flush left and the other heads are centered. Column and row heads use sentence case. Row subheadings are indented 1 em. Model names are capitalized (Model 1). A multi-part table uses Panel A and Panel B; Table 1A and Table 1B are not allowed (renumber them instead).
tables.font_size: not specified for tables. Body text is 11-pt.
tables.landscape: allowed as a last resort with the informs4 rotate environment. Try a smaller type size or restructuring first.

figures.formats: Line art, charts and diagrams: PDF, EPS, SVG or Adobe Illustrator (vector). Photos and screenshots: TIFF, PNG or high-quality JPEG. Microsoft Office figures may be supplied as the native Word, Excel or PowerPoint files. BMP is not acceptable (older INFORMS instructions). Figure source files are required at acceptance.
figures.resolution: Raster images at 300 dpi, sized close to print size; they are converted to CMYK or grayscale. Scanned line art at 900 dpi or more (informs4 documentation). Images copied at low resolution from the web, slides or screenshots may be rejected.
figures.vector_preferred: yes: graphs and drawings should be editable vector files (EPS, PDF). Pasting Office graphs via the clipboard creates bitmaps and should be avoided.
figures.color: Color appears online; print is grayscale unless the authors pay per color page (INFORMS FAQ and file-preparation page). Captions get a '(Color online)' prefix in production. Figures must stay understandable in grayscale, and color must not be the only carrier of meaning. Color figures cannot replace black-and-white ones once in production.
figures.fonts: Standard fonts, embedded, with no custom fonts. Labels and lines must stay legible when the figure is reduced to page size. No minimum point size is stated. Axis labels are not bold.
figures.dimensions: not specified (submit close to the intended printed size)
figures.caption: Title case after a bold number with a period ('Figure 1. Example of Display Used in Experiment 2'), with no final period. Sentences after the first become 'Note.' or 'Notes.'; 'Source.' comes first. In informs4 the caption position (above or below) is set automatically by the journal option; the INFORMS sample places it above the art. Cite as 'Figure 1' with 'Figure' spelled out.
figures.panels: Lowercase letters in parentheses: Figure 2(a), or 'panel (a) of Figure 2'. Write 'Figure 2, (a) and (b)', not 'Figures 2(a) and 2(b)'. informs4 uses subcaption with parenthesized subrefs, sans-serif labels and footnotesize.
figures.placement: Embedded in the manuscript (template floats). The MNSC page itself was not read directly.
figures.notes: Below the figure, with the italic heading 'Note.' or 'Notes.'; a 'Source.' line comes first. Running text inside the figure is moved into the Note during copyediting.
figures.other_rules: The Author Portal also asks authors to use figures and graphs to summarize key results and to explain models and algorithms. No rules on 3D charts, gridlines or legends.
